jurisdiction.name: Uganda
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Uganda has no AI-specific law or strategy yet. AI is covered by the Data Protection and Privacy Act 2019, which gives rights over automated decision-taking, and the 2020 National Fourth Industrial Revolution Strategy. A 2025 national AI landscape assessment by the ICT ministry and the ITU, which proposes an AI risk management framework, feeds a National AI and Emerging Technologies Strategy and an AI framework that are still being developed.
lead_institutions: Ministry of ICT and National Guidance
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from documents on the ICT ministry's website. The Uganda Gazette has no searchable online portal and the data protection office's site has no document listing. The national AI strategy, the AI framework and the 2021 data protection regulations are tracked as leads. As a country of over 20 million people with few records, Uganda is marked for a longer catch-up pass.

instruments.official_title: The Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of Uganda (assented to by the President on 25 February 2019)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of ICT and National Guidance
instruments.current_status: In force. The copy on the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance 'Acts and Laws' page is the assented Act (date of assent 25 February 2019 handwritten on the assent page); it does not state the commencement date, so effective_date is left null. The Act now appears in the revised laws as Cap. 97. Its implementing Data Protection and Privacy Regulations, 2021 and proposals to amend the Act to address AI are held as leads.
instruments.summary: Uganda's general data protection law, binding on public bodies and private data collectors, processors and controllers; it sets data protection principles, consent, purpose limitation, security and breach-notification duties, and creates the Personal Data Protection Office under the National Information Technology Authority - Uganda (the 'Authority'). Section 27 gives data subjects rights in relation to automated decision-taking: they may require that significant decisions are not based solely on automated processing, must be notified when such a decision is taken, and may require reconsideration within 21 days, with complaints to the Authority. These provisions are the main existing legal rules applying to AI systems that process personal data in Uganda.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only enacted law with an explicit automated decision-making provision (s. 27); governs personal data used to train and run AI.
metadata_gaps: Commencement date not stated in the assented copy read

instruments.official_title: Uganda's National 4IR Strategy: A continental 4IR hub that enables a smart and connected Ugandan society (Executive Summary)
instruments.english_title: Uganda's National Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) Strategy (Executive Summary)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of ICT and National Guidance, developed by the National Expert Taskforce on the Fourth Industrial Revolution established by the President in 2018
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of ICT and National Guidance
instruments.current_status: Only the executive summary is published on the Ministry's 'Strategies and Frameworks' page; the summary itself carries no date, and the year 2020 is taken from the Ministry/ITU 'Uganda national AI landscape assessment', which cites it as 'Uganda National 4IR Strategy, 2020'. It is the existing umbrella strategy for AI and other 4IR technologies; a dedicated National AI & Emerging Technologies Strategy was under consultation in 2026 (see leads).
instruments.summary: Uganda's national strategy for Fourth Industrial Revolution technologies, including AI, blockchain, IoT and cloud computing, prepared on the advice of the presidential National Expert Taskforce on the 4IR with the vision of a continental 4IR hub and a smart and connected Ugandan society. It identifies domain opportunities (e.g. AI diagnostics in health, AI-based tax compliance and agriculture applications) and five critical enablers: 4IR connectivity, agile governance, an upskilled population, eGovernment and local innovation. Under 'regulatory agility' it prioritises data legislation and regulation and calls for equipping regulators to respond quickly, allow experimentation with new technologies and close legislative and regulatory gaps created by 4IR technologies.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current umbrella strategy covering AI; precursor to the National AI & Emerging Technologies Strategy under development.
metadata_gaps: Exact publication or adoption date not stated on the document (year from the Ministry/ITU AI landscape assessment)
Full strategy text not published; only the executive summary

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of ICT and National Guidance and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), under the joint project 'Technical Assistance and Training to Uganda on National ICT Development Strategy' (2021-2024)
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of ICT and National Guidance
instruments.current_status: Published in 2025 (ITU copyright 2025, ISBN 978-92-61-40291-4) and listed on the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance 'Reports' page, with a foreword by the Minister of ICT and National Guidance. Its recommendations (AI policy, strategy and legal framework) feed the National AI & Emerging Technologies Strategy under development.
instruments.summary: Government assessment of Uganda's AI readiness, prepared by the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance with ITU through a baseline survey of public and private AI actors, stakeholder consultations, benchmarking against Rwanda, Kenya and the United States, and an assessment of government infrastructure and skills for AI-enabled e-services. It finds gaps in AI infrastructure, skills, curricula and the absence of an AI policy, legal and regulatory framework. It proposes an AI risk management framework (risk matrix, legal and standards-based approaches, governance, risk identification, assessment, monitoring and reporting) and recommends that the Government develop an AI policy, strategy and legal and regulatory framework, invest in high-performance computing and use public-private partnerships.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Official AI readiness assessment with a proposed national AI risk management framework; basis for the forthcoming AI strategy.
metadata_gaps: Only the year (2025) is stated; no month or launch date

organizations.name: Ministry of ICT and National Guidance
organizations.ai_governance_role: Lead ministry for ICT and AI policy. Publishes the National 4IR Strategy (2020) and, with ITU, the Uganda national AI landscape assessment; is developing a National AI & Emerging Technologies Strategy and an Artificial Intelligence Framework (listed in its 2025/26-2029/30 strategic plan). The Minister responsible for ICT is the minister under the Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019.

organizations.ai_governance_role: Enacted the Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019, which includes rights in relation to automated decision-taking (section 27). No AI bill found.
